chapter: Gulf Coast bands and early jobs
title: Smoking marijuana in the 1920s, bought on St. Philip Street
summary: Recalls how marijuana was bought through a hole in a wall, then then-illegal status and price.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: But I get them confused. But we were there together. You know what you said when they were passing the sensor around with all the smoke coming out of it? What? I don't know if we should put this on tape of the other. Go ahead. But you said if it had been grass, Tony would have gotten up in smoke smoke.
You see, There is no generation gap.
If you want to get it, if you want to talk a little bit about smoking grass, those days was, it's so different than it is today that it's pitiful. It was a sin to smoke grass when I smoked grass.
So nobody hardly ever did but just us.

Today, it's the most public thing in the world. I have seen doctors go out and puff it with musicians. I know. I know good and well. I don't do it anymore, but I'm fooled with it because it's no good anymore.
Well, where did you get it? Way back when you were a young musician and used to smoke it. Where would you...

You could go on St. Philip Street in the 500 block and you go into the men's room. Uh-huh. And there was a little hole in the wall about that big and another little hole in the wall. You knocked on the wall. A finger went through the hole. You put your finger in the hole for the size of the stick that you wanted. If you bought a single, it was 15 cents. If you bought a... They called it... Let me see. What did they call it? A double, I believe. It was 20 cents. And it was three times as big as these that you pay $2 for a day. and that this today is absolutely no good because they never do wait until it matures to pick it. And there wasn't ever known at that time for it to ever be grown anywhere in the United States that I ever heard of. It was all strictly Mexican. Not even Colombia.
